blocks.text: JEDUTHUN, “THE KING’S SEER” (2 CHRONICLES 35:15) · UNITED KINGDOM
Jeduthun. A head of David's singers who “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD”.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophesied with harps
ERA
United kingdom c. 1050–930 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
David · Solomon
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
He “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD”.
THE CALL
How the word came
He “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD”. 1 Chronicles 25:3
Chronicles calls him “Jeduthun the king’s seer”. 2 Chronicles 35:15
The titles of Psalms 39, 62 and 77 read “To the chief Musician, to Jeduthun” or “even to Jeduthun”. Psalms 39:1 Psalms 62:1 Psalms 77:1
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before two kings
KING OF JUDAH, THEN OF ALL ISRAEL
David
“under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the LORD.”
1 Chronicles 25:3 (KJV) →
KING OF ALL ISRAEL
Solomon
THE SONGS
What he sang
Thanks and praise
PLACES
Where his story happened
Gibeon · Before the tabernacle in the high place
SIGNS
Signs and wonders
WONDER
The cloud at the temple's dedication
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Heman
Asaph
Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, his sons
Obed-edom “the son of Jeduthun”
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS

From the textScripture does not tell of his death. Sons of Jeduthun were among the Levites who cleansed the house of the LORD under Hezekiah, Josiah's singers kept the order of “David, and Asaph, and Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer”, and a descendant of Jeduthun served in Jerusalem after the exile. 2 Chronicles 29:12–15 2 Chronicles 35:15 Nehemiah 11:17
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Yes, two names for one man
John Gill (1748–1763); Ellicott's commentary (c. 1878–1884); E. G. Hirsch and E. König, Jewish Encyclopedia (1903)

Ethan stands beside Heman and Asaph in 1 Chronicles 6 and 15, and Jeduthun in the same place in 1 Chronicles 16 and 25; Gill writes “Jeduthun; or Ethan”, and the Jewish Encyclopedia speaks of “Ethan-Jeduthun”. The site's person data also treats them as one. 1 Chronicles 6:44 1 Chronicles 15:17 1 Chronicles 16:41 1 Chronicles 25:1 [27][9][44]
Two families' traditions
W. E. Barnes (1899)
“Probably there was a variation in the tradition as to the third name, two families competing each for the honour of its own ancestor.” 1 Chronicles 16:41 [104]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 11
1 Chronicles 6 1 Chronicles 15 1 Chronicles 16 1 Chronicles 25 2 Chronicles 5 2 Chronicles 29 2 Chronicles 35 Nehemiah 11 Psalms 39 Psalms 62 Psalms 77
PASSAGES · 11
1 Chronicles 6:44–47 1 Chronicles 15:17–19 1 Chronicles 16:38–42 1 Chronicles 25:1–6 2 Chronicles 5:12–13 2 Chronicles 29:14 2 Chronicles 35:15 Nehemiah 11:17 Psalms 39:1 Psalms 62:1 Psalms 77:1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
1 Chronicles 25:3 says Jeduthun had “six” sons but the King James text names five.
No words of Jeduthun are quoted, and Scripture does not say he wrote any psalm.
Whether Obed-edom “the son of Jeduthun” (1 Chronicles 16:38) is the Obed-edom the Gittite who kept the ark (2 Samuel 6:10) is not said.
